findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The dish machine was observed to be sanitizing at 0ppm of Chlorine. CORRECTED- The inspector primed the sanitizer and the dish machine was observed to sanitize at 100ppm of Chlorine. This was discussed with the PIC. The dish machine should be being tested daily using the Chlorine test strips that are available in the facility. A spot check will be conducted to ensure that the dish machine is sanitizing at a label-recommended concentration.
findings.citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The sanitizer bucket on the cook-line was observed to be at 50ppm of Quaternary ammonium. The sanitizer bucket was remade and tested to be at 0ppm of Quaternary ammonium. CORRECTED- The bucket was remade by the PIC and tested to be at 400ppm of Quaternary ammonium. Ensure that the sanitizer dispenser knob is being fully turned when filling up a sanitizer bucket. These buckets should be changed at least every two to four hours (more if they are heavily used) and should be frequently tested to ensure that they are at a label-recommended concentration. Staff should be trained on how to properly make a sanitizer bucket, how to test it, and how often to change them.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: The facility uses white containers that are placed in the freezer and then are used to cold hold along the cook-line. Cheese in one of these containers was probed to be at 57F and 49F. Onions that are cooked and cooled were probed to be at 66F in another one of these containers. These containers should be changed out more or another method of cold holding will be needed. CORRECTED- The white containers were switched with new ones from the freezer and the cheese and onions had only been in the previous containers for a short period of time. A spot check will be conducted to ensure that TCS food items are being properly cold held.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels.

The paper towel dispenser at the hand sinks next to the three part sink would not produce paper towels during this inspection. The PICs were told and replaced the paper towels to correct the violation. Ensure that all hand sinks are properly supplied at all times.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

The sanitizer dispenser is not consistently producing sanitizer of correct concentration. The PICs are currently making a solution manually using a CL based sanitizer. A follow up is being set for 10 days to ensure repairs are made.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. 

1) The floor under and behind the soda syrups in the dry storage area are in need of cleaning; 2) dust has accumulated on the tubes of the walk in cooler’s fan unit; 3) the floor around and behind the ice machine is in need of cleaning. findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. 

Mops are observed stored with the heads pooled up in the mop sink. The PIC was shown and moved the mops so that the heads could hang dry. Education was conducted. Ensure regardless of equipment the bristles or the heads are stored so that they are able to hang and drip dry efficiently.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Inspector observed that the soda nozzles at the drive up soda fountain are heavily soiled with mold. These items shall be properly cleaned and sanitized at least once every 24 hours. The soda fountain was closed, nozzles removed and properly washed rinsed and sanitized. Nozzles were placed onto the machine with clean, gloved hands. Treat the soda nozzles just like a fork, knife or spoon. The violation is considered corrected on site. Maintain the soda fountain nozzles clean and sanitized. 

4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above. 

Hot dogs in the hot holding unit are 109F. The unit keeps breaking the circuit and they have replaced the hot dogs several times already today. Be diligent about checking the hot dog temperatures if continuing to use this unit. The hot dogs should be checked on the hour and discarded if the temperature is below 135F. Hot dogs were discarded and replaced with new hot dogs.

The facility has had an electrician there to replace 2 or 3 plugs already and have more GFI plugs on order from Bromida that will be installed when they arrive.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.  

Observed manager begin to put a soiled cheese sauce nozzle onto the new bag of cheese sauce for the Gehl’s machine. The manager was stopped and questioned on the procedure. She said that the other nozzle was broken. She then went to wash the nozzle that was removed from the discarded cheese sauce that was holding at 104F.  Discussed the need to clean and sanitizer food contact surfaces. Violation considered corrected on site.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

Observed two employees change gloves and do hand washing but not use a clean barrier to properly turn off the faucet handles. The employees were coached at the time of inspection. Take every opportunity to train proper hand washing. The violation is considered corrected on site.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-304.11: (A) FOOD shall only contact surfaces of EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS that are cleaned. (B) SINGLE-SERVICE/USE ARTICLES (C) LINENS 

Observed a breakfast sandwich from another facility to be stuffed into the hot dog steamer. The outside of the bag was in contact with hot dogs in the steamer. Twenty hot dogs were discarded as they had come into contact with an unclean surface during  storage. Do not use the hot dog steamer as a personal sandwich hot holding device.  It is important to protect food from possible contamination at all times. The violation is considered corrected on site.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above. 

Observed that half of a bag of cheese sauce, that was hot held in the Gehl’s machine overnight, to be 104F.  The Bag was discarded and a new bag was placed into the holder. The holding unit for the cheese sauce did not have a part of the heat shield properly attached to it. This part helps hold the heat in properly. Verify the temperature of hot held cheese every morning upon arrival to the facility and watch the internal thermometer throughout the day to ensure that the food is being maintained in the safe temperature range. The machine thermometer was reading 140F at the end of the inspection. The violation is considered corrected on site.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
4-903.11: (A) clean EQUIPMENT and clean ARTICLES shall be stored in clean, dry location where they are not exposed to contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination. 

Observed single use utensils at the service window to be stored in a holder that is not covered. This container contains crumbs and food soil in the bottom. Clean the utensil holding unit and maintain it free of crumbs and food debris.

findings.comment:

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.  

(REPEAT) Observed several employees attempt to go between tasks (moving boxes, moving dust pan and broom, etc) with gloved hands, remove gloves, don new gloves, and not properly wash hands. Discussed with employees. When entering a kitchen to engage in food service or when changing tasks and gloves, employees must appropriately wash hands. Ensure hot water, soap, and paper towel use. Utilize a barrier to turn off the faucet handles after washing hands (paper towel) in order to inhibit cross contamination. COS. This is a repeat violations since the last routine inspections on 1/31/22 and 5/4/22.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

Observed the dish machine to be 0 ppm after multiple test runs. Facility has bleach test strips. PIC changed the sanitizer component of the dish machine - low. 200 ppm once corrected. Discussed if corporate policy exists for checking sanitizer levels with test strips several times a day. It is a part of daily tasks and should be done 1-2x daily. PIC was not at the facility this morning. Ensure staff is aware to test all sanitizer buckets, 3 compartment sink sanitizer, and dish machine for appropriate levels of sanitizer. Quat - 200 to 400 ppm. Bleach/chlorine - 50 to 200 ppm. Test strips are available in the office area. Educate staff on proper test strip use and different types of sanitizer. Bleach is only utilized at the dish machine at this facility, other methods are quaternary ammonium based. COS.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions. 

Observed many drain flies under the hand sink area by the drive thru (open base cabinet). Ice cream prep area is directly next to this area. PIC indicated she will call Orkin to address the issue. Inspector will follow-up on 11/21/22.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. 

(REPEAT) Observed the following non-food contact areas to be in need of cleaning:
1. Both walk-in cooler and freezer fans have accumulation of dust. Wash, rinse, sanitize fans as needed to prevent dust build-up. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 5/4/22.
2. The ceiling above the prep line has dust build-up, as well as the vents. Clean the area.
3. Flooring under the dry storage metal shelving carts has layer of grime and various single service utensils/food debris under them. Pull out the shelving and clean the floor.
4. Prep cooler vents (both the one with the base not being utilized and the main prep cooler for burger prep) have layer of dust on grates. Clean dust.
5. Various reach-in coolers and freezers need cleaned of food splash and food debris at the base and walls, as well as grates of shelving within them: customer reach-in freezer for custard, reach-in cooler near shake maker, fries reach-in freezer.

Ensure routine cleaning of non-food contact surface to prevent food debris build-up, dust accumulation, and general grime. Discussed with PIC.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

Observed the following areas in need of repairs:
1. Handsink near the vegetable wash station (across from burger prep line) has caulking coming away from the interior creases of the handsink. Re-caulk.
2. The dish machine area has moldy water build-up along the caulking, as well as the wall behind the dish machine. Wash, rinse, sanitize the wall and re-caulk the moldy caulk. Ensure the caulk at the 3 compartment sink is also re-caulked if needed from moldy caulk.
3. Mop sink needs re-caulked due to moldy caulk. There is a piece of edging missing at the mop sink (broken). Repair the trim. 

Discussed repairs with PIC. Ensure repairs before next routine inspection.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

Observed several food handlers licenses to be expired. Observed multiple signed employee health reporting agreements, but no matching food handlers licenses to the employees. Update the public health binder so all employee food handlers license copies are in the binder. Employees should complete the training within 30 days of employment. Discussed with PIC.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

(REPEAT) Observed allergen training certification for all CFPM’s to be expired (4-5 people). Public health binder has the educational page regarding where to take the course online. Allergen training certification must be completed by all CFPM’s and re-done every 3 years. Discussed with PIC. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 5/4/22.

findings.comment:
4-703.11: After cleaning, FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be SANITIZED in: (A) manual hot water operations. (B) mechanical hot water operations. (C) Chemical manual or mechanical operations. Contact times shall be consistent with those on EPA-registered label use – standard contact time 30 seconds. 

Observed dish washer improperly sanitizing food-contact items. Dish washer was combining soap and sanitizer, rather than just using sanitizer in the 3rd basin of the 3 compartment sink. Testing this combination provided 0 ppm. After some education, testing just sanitizer in the 3rd basin proved to be 400 ppm. Cease the combination of wash/sanitizer products together. This is not meet contact times or sanitization levels. COS.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.112: Dead or trapped birds, insects, rodents, and other pests shall be removed from control devices and the PREMISES at a frequency that prevents their accumulation, decomposition, or the attraction of pests. 

Observed multiple sticky fly traps to be full (hanging away from food-contact surfaces). Ensure routine changing of fly traps in order to hinder accumulation of dead pests.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-101.19: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. 

(REPEAT) Observed ponding water within walk-in freezer. Water is freezing into an accumulation on floor and on cooling unit. Discussed repairs with PIC. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 6/3/21.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. 

Observed the following nonfood-contact surfaces in need of cleaning:
1. Both spray nozzles near the dish machine and 3 compartment sink had accumulation of food debris and mold on top of and under the nozzle.
2. Fan running near the burger prep area has dust.

Ensure routine cleaning - wash, rinse, sanitize.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.comment:
5-205.15: A PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW; P and (B) Maintained in good repair. 

Observed back hand sink near the 3 compartment sink to not be flowing water and have a drip when turned on. Water is not dispensing correctly. Sink is not being utilized at this time. Ensure repairs to hand sink by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

(REPEAT) Observed the following areas to no longer be smooth and easily cleanable: 
1. Caulk at the dish machine area is not present. Re-caulk this area. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 6/3/21.
2. Multiple broken tiles between fryer and French fry hold holding unit. Repair tiles.

Ensure repairs before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Observed interior of dish machine to have heavy accumulation of debris and lime build-up. Discussed routine cleaning of the interior of dish machine. PIC was in agreement to utilize de-limer and scrub the inside of the dish machine. Inspector will follow-up on 6/14/21.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-101.19: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. 

Observed ponding water at the base of the walk-in freezer - created large block of ice. Repair walk-in freezer so ponding, frozen water does not occur and build-up. Ensure repairs by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed
findings.comment:
5-403.12: Condensate drainage and other non-SEWAGE liquids and rainwater shall be drained from point of discharge to disposal according to LAW. 

Observed ponding water at the base of the raw hamburger prep cooler near the grill. Employee stated that the water was not from hamburger thawing, but instead dripping from the inside vent of the reach-in cooler. Ensure repairs before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

Observed caulk at the dish machine to be molding and coming away from the wall. Re-caulk the dish machine before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114  (P) Quaternary ammonium sanitizer measured 100 ppm at various sanitization buckets in kitchen. Maintain concentration at 200 ppm to 400 ppm as indicated on manufacturer's label. Reference 4-501.114.

Observed multiple sanitization buckets in kitchen to register with 100 ppm of quaternary ammonium. Discussed routine changing of buckets in order to ensure accurate concentraiton of quat - 200 to 400 ppm. PIC was in compliance and changed buckets during inspection. New concentrations registered 400 ppm. COS.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.citation_text:
4-101.19  (C) Nonfood-contact surfaces of walk-in freezer is no longer easily cleanable.  Reference 4-101.19.

Observed large accumulation of ice within walk-in freezer. PIC indicated that this is a routine finding - staff must clean out ice nightly. Discussed repairs with PIC.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13  (C) Soil residue present on both spray nozzles at dish machine and 3 compartments sink. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

Observed both spray nozzles of 3 compartment sink and dish machine to have large accumulations of debris. Discussed routine cleaning of nonfood-contact surfaces with PIC.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-201.11  (C) Caulk at 3 compartment sink and floor plate of walk-in cooler were found in a state of disrepair, or not to be smooth and easily cleanable. Except as specified in Section 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are smooth and easily cleanable.  Reference 6-201.11.

Observed caulk at 3 compartment sink to be coming from wall and sink. Floor plate as entering walk-in cooler observed to be deformed and presenting cleaning issues (REPEAT). Discussed repairs with PIC.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12  (P) Food employee was observed to not use a clean barrier to turn off the faucet after washing hands and prior to handling food. Inspector discussed with the PIC and instructed education for employees.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114  (P) The dish machine at the facility registered at 0 ppm CL on the inspectors test strips during the inspection. PIC contacted Ecolab during the inspection for maintenance. They did not arrive prior to the inspector leaving. The three part sink was prepared to serve as the sanitizing step and is at 400 ppm Quat. Inspector will spot check to ensure maintenance is conducted on the dish machine.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text: 4-302.14  (Pf) A test kit for the sanitizer used by the dish machine was not available during the inspection. PIC was instructed to maintain test kits for each sanitizer used in the facility.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.citation_text: 5-205.15  (C) The hand sink in the men's bathroom is constantly flowing and unable to turn off during the inspection. PIC was instructed to consult a licensed plumber for repairs.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text: 6-201.11  (C) 1) The floor plate as you enter the walk in cooler was observed deformed and presenting a cleaning issue. The caulking around the hand sink in the men's bathroom was observed cracking. PIC was instructed to repair prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment: Observed the hand sink next to the three compartment sink to not have any paper towels installed in the dispenser. Paper towels were provided during the inspection. 6-301.12  (Pf) Disposable paper towels not provided at the hand washing sink. Provide disposable paper towels at hand washing sinks. Reference 6-301.12.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment: 1) Observed the ice bin at the drive thru to be stored open when not in use and a single service lid in the ice bin. Lid was removed and ice bin was pulled closed. 2) Observed the custard machine to not have the covers over the bins after being filled. Covers were placed on during the inspection. 3-307.11  (C)  Food shall be protected from contamination. Reference 3-307.11.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment: Observed the dipper wells where the spatulas for cutting the custard are stored to not be on and spatulas stored in standing water. Dipper wells were turned on during the inspection. Keep dipper wells on when storing in use utensils. 3-304.12  (C)  Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 °F. Reference 3-304.12.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment: Observed single service items stored in the cabinet underneath the soda fountain in the dining room where the drain lines run. Do not store single service items in this area. Store them in the cabinets that do not have drain lines/wastewater running through them. 4-903.12 (C)  Single-Use Articles may not be stored in: 1) locker rooms; 2) toilet rooms; 3) dressing rooms; 4) garbage rooms; 5) mechanical rooms; 6) under non shielded sewer lines; 7) under leaking water lines; 8) under open stairwells; 9) under other sources of contamination. Reference 4-903.12.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed no time control policy being implemented during the inspection. Make sure to always have time marked on items and use within four hours.
750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above)

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.comment:
Observed chili at 125 F. The chili was discarded because the manager could not tell me what time or how long it has been out of temperature.
750-150(b)  Hot potentially hazardous foods shall be maintained at 135°F or above except during the cooling process. Store hot foods at 135°F or above. (Except for rare roast beef which may be held at 130F.)

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
Observed food stored underneath plumbing. The food was moved. Make sure to never store food under plumbing.
750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
Observed the Freddy's seasoning to have a single service cup stored in the container. This is not a proper practice. All bulk containers should have a scoop with the handle extended out of the food.
750-280 Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed ponding water on the floor in the dish area. Make sure to clean floors as needed.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Lighting provided as required.  Fixtures shielded
findings.comment:
Observed a missing light shield in the dry storage. Replace the light shield.
750-1240 All lights in the food prep, food storage or kitchen area of a establishment must be properly shielded (i.e. either have a physical shield or be a shatter resistant bulb) so as to reduce the potential for cross contamination in case of breakage.  Provide properly shielded lights.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: 1) (REPEAT) Observed cheesecake bites that need to be held 41F or below. They were 60 F holding. 2) (REPEAT) Observed grilled onions to be out of temperature with no time control. The manager stated that onions were put out around 12. Make sure to time mark onions.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
Observed candy toppings stored underneath the plumbing of handwashing sink. This is not a proper practice.
750-130(d) All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store ready to eat foods above or a way from raw foods.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
Observed lids stored on the floor. Make sure all food and single service items are properly stored at all times.
750-880 Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water disposed properly
findings.comment:
Observed wastewater in the mop bucket in the back of the establishment. Dump mop water as soon as the task is complete.
750-1050 All water containing sewage shall be disposed of  properly either by a public sewage system or an approved private disposal system which is constructed and operated in conformance with applicable State and local laws, ordinances and regulations.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
1) (REPEAT) A tile is cracked on the floor in front of the dish machine. It was repaired but has broken again. Repair tiles to make the floor smooth and easily cleanable. 2) (REPEAT) Observed the walk in cooler floor to be rusty. It has been deep cleaned since last inspection but should be smooth and easily cleanable.
750-1200 All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean floors.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment:
Observed no certified IL FSSMC during the inspection. Provide a certified food manager for next routine inspection.
750-540 All Category I facilities must employ an adequate number of  Licensed Food Service Sanitation Managers to have one present at all times food is being prepared to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide an adequate number of  Food Service Sanitation Manager.
